name: Spring
description: A spring tank: one to three dispersive springs whose echoes chirp and drip, with a transformer drive in front.

params.name: Mix
params.description: Balance between the dry signal and the springs. Fully up is the springs alone.

params.name: Decay
params.description: How long the springs keep ringing. The top end always dies away a little faster than the rest.

params.name: Tension
params.description: How the springs chirp. Slack makes every echo a long audible sweep; taut gives tight slaps with a short whip at the top.

params.name: Springs
params.description: One spring sits in the centre. Two puts a spring on each side, and Three adds a third in the middle for a denser tail.

params.name: Tone
params.description: Low-pass on the spring sound. Lower is darker and softens the chirp; higher lets the splash through.

params.name: Drip
params.description: Feeds extra treble into the springs so attacks splash, as on the classic outboard units.

params.name: Pre-delay
params.description: The gap before the springs answer, which keeps the start of the sound clear of the splash.

params.name: Drive
params.description: How hard the input pushes the tank's transformer. Low is clean; high saturates loud passages before they reach the springs.

params.name: Width
params.description: Stereo width of the spring sound only. Zero is mono and full is widest. With one spring there is nothing to widen.

origin.note: Written for live-mix on cpp/kit after the parametric spring model of Valimaki, Parker and Abel (JAES 2010): each spring is a feedback delay loop dispersed by a cascade of 100 first-order allpasses stretched to a transition frequency, here run at a reduced sample rate as in their efficient form. The low-frequency chirp structure only; not a model of any particular tank.
